[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call then we'll dive in, we have Priya from SE, and I got the performance slides up.
[00:16] Tom: Hi, Tom here. Sara and Raj and Maya are on. good to go.
[00:22] Priya: Hey all. excited to run through the results we ran this week.
[00:28] Jordan: Cool. Agenda  one, walk through the model eval table, two, discuss pinning and fallback, three, security asks, four, next steps.
[00:38] Priya: Quick refresher: we evaluated two candidates from the catalog, Redwood-rlf-1.2 (lightweight) and Redwood-rlf-2.0 (higher quality), also compared to a baseline Anthropic-ish model the team has been using. Results are in the shared sheet link  I sent it earlier.
[01:02] Sara: I saw the sheet. the numbers looked better for 2.0 on tricky prompts but cost was higher.
[01:10] Priya: Right. Highlights: p95 latency on hosted Redwood-rlf-1.2 is ~210ms, p95 for 2.0 is about 360ms. Token cost per completed request (avg tokens ~120) is roughly $0.004 for 1.2 and $0.009 for 2.0 in our pilot config. Quality (human eval, accuracy on slot-filling tasks) is 78% for 1.2 and 89% for 2.0.
[01:44] Raj: Those are good numbers. what's the live traffic pattern? are we seeing a lot of long-context requests?
[01:50] Tom: Our snippets are mostly short, median 60 tokens, tail up to 800 during some bulk queries.
[01:58] Priya: That tail is why we saw higher p95s on 2.0  kernel selection and kv cache warmup matter. worth noting we saw some stray transcribes where 'KV cache' got logged as 'KV cash' in the trace  auto-transcription artifact.
[02:14] Jordan: For pinning, we recommend pinning production to Redwood-rlf-1.2 as the initial stable variant and using 2.0 as a canary for higher-quality routes, or vice versa depending on SLA. The main choices: pin to 1.2 for lower cost / lower latency; pin to 2.0 for higher quality.
[02:34] Sara: Our goal is to minimize regressions for customer-facing completions. if 2.0 improves critical flows, would prefer 2.0 even if more expensive.
[02:44] Tom: Cost matters  we're watching unit economics closely. can we do automatic fallback to 1.2 when latency SLOs are breached?
[02:51] Priya: Yes, Redwood supports smart routing and fallback to compatible variants. We can set thresholds  e.g., p95 > 400ms triggers fallback from 2.0 to 1.2 for that route. Also can config canary windows and automatic rollback triggers if quality drops (we rely on your eval prompt set for comparisons).
[03:12] Raj: On security, two quick items: 1) we need confirmation on KMS/HSM support for keys and 2) audit log retention for 12 months. Are those available for the Private deployment?
[03:25] Jordan: Yes, Private and Dedicated tiers include KMS integrations and longer audit retention. For hosted we support customer-managed KMS via our VPC private control plane option too; I'll attach the doc.
[03:37] Maya: Also SSO and SCIM for user sync  do we have SAML?
[03:42] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, and RBAC roles can be set per team. We'll flag the SSO doc in the follow-ups.
[03:52] Sara: Back to pinning  what's the rollout flow? say we pin to 2.0 for a small percentage, run it for a week, then roll to 100% if metrics look good  can we automatically rollback if quality drops?
[04:04] Priya: Yes, rollout policies can be canary-based with automatic rollback. You define success metrics  e.g., no more than 2% regression on our eval set, or absolute thresholds on error rates and latency. If a canary exceeds thresholds, the system drops it back to the previous pinned variant and notifies your team.
[04:22] Tom: For our eval set, we need to be sure it's representative; we'll send 3 prompt buckets: transactional, product info, and edge-case returns.
[04:34] Jordan: Great. For the A/B we propose running 10% of traffic on the canary for two days or until 5k requests, whichever comes first, then evaluate. Priya will run the load test to verify scaling.
[04:49] Priya: On rollback triggers  we can also set token-cost budgets so if the canary would push cost >X% we can cap it. that helps you avoid runaway spend.
[05:00] Raj: Good. On encryption  we need to confirm in-transit and at-rest guarantees and whether logs contain PII. Also audit granularity.
[05:12] Jordan: In-transit TLS yes, at-rest encryption with KMS, and audit logs can be filtered for PII masking. We'll send the security pack and the SOC two summary.
[05:24] Tom: Are there any known perf regressions between model versions that we should watch for  like thread contention or GPU kernel issues?
[05:31] Priya: Occasionally certain sequence lengths trigger different kernel paths which move latency. Our runtime picks kernels based on sequence distribution; that's why profiling with your real snippets is critical. In a few runs we saw a spike at around 600 token sequences for 2.0  that was KV warmup + a less-optimal kernel path. We can recommend micro-batching tweaks or quantization to help.
[05:56] Sara: Would quantizing 2.0 help the p95 enough to justify its quality gains?
[06:01] Priya: Possibly  our Optimize team can run a quick quantization pass; tradeoffs include slight quality delta. We'll flag recommended quant profiles.
[06:10] Jordan: Operationally, our recommended default for this pilot: pin production to rlf-1.2, route high-value routes (checkout, returns) to canary rlf-2.0 with 10% traffic, enable fallback to 1.2 at p95 > 400ms, set cost cap for canary, and run the 10k-user load test. If after A/B the quality delta warrants it, consider switching full production to 2.0 with quant profile.
[06:42] Tom: Sounds good. Can we get a concrete example of the rollback rule syntax?
[06:47] Priya: We'll attach the runbook snippet. e.g., "canary.p95 > 400ms for 5 consecutive minutes -> rollback" and "eval.regression > 2% on prompt_set_A -> rollback".
[07:02] Raj: For compliance we also need the ability to run an on-prem deployment if required later. timeline?
[07:09] Jordan: On-prem is doable but takes lead time  for pilot we recommend Dedicated with VPC and KMS; we'll discuss Private/on-prem during contract talks if needed.
[07:19] Maya: Next steps recap?
[07:22] Jordan: I'll go first  Jordan will send pinned model config, canary plan, pricing delta estimates, and the security pack by Friday 2027-05-06.
[07:31] Priya: I'll provision the 10k-user load test and run the canary scenario, and share results; target run by 2027-05-11. Also I'll prepare the pinning + fallback runbook.
[07:41] Tom: We'll send the three prompt buckets and the traffic distribution by 2027-05-07 and validate results.
[07:48] Raj: I'll compile KMS and audit log questions and send by 2027-05-06.
[07:54] Jordan: Any blockers?
[07:56] Sara: none from engineering. just want to make sure the rollback thresholds are conservative.
[08:02] Priya: We'll default to conservative thresholds in the runbook  you can tighten later.
[08:07] Jordan: Alright, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the sheet and runbook links.
[08:12] Tom: Thanks.
[08:14] Jordan: Meeting adjourned.
